landmarks.name: Pendjari National Park
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve known for its diverse wildlife including elephants, lions, and hippos.

landmarks.name: Royal Palaces of Abomey
landmarks.writeup: Historic palaces of the Kingdom of Dahomey, showcasing traditional architecture and cultural heritage.

landmarks.name: Ouidah Museum of History
landmarks.writeup: Museum dedicated to the history of the transatlantic slave trade and Benin's cultural past.

cultural_events.name: Voodoo Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Annual celebration honoring the traditional Vodun religion with rituals, music, and dance.

cultural_events.name: Ganvie Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Festival in the lake village of Ganvie celebrating the unique stilt village culture.

food_writeup: Beninese cuisine features staple foods like maize, rice, yams, and cassava, often served with spicy sauces and stews made from peanuts, tomatoes, and local vegetables.
brief_history: Benin, formerly known as Dahomey, was a powerful kingdom before becoming a French colony in the 19th century. It gained independence in 1960 and has since developed a stable democratic government.

important_people.name: Mathieu Kérékou
important_people.description: Former President and influential political figure

current_conflicts: Benin is generally stable with no significant internal or external conflicts reported as of 2024.
